evidence.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.002, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8
This card has 138 earlier purchases billed to region 476 (first on 2016-07-03)

The alert's score (0.53, as in the case record) differs from the score stored on the transaction (0.05). Two bank sources disagree, and neither moves the decision: the bank warns its model is near useless for January, so its score is not used as evidence
